ratiosYieldCapacity: Two pounds sunchokes, restored ¼ cup roast oil, eight garlic cloves/four thyme sprigs discarded, two tablespoons starting butter, ¼ cup raw cider vinegar reduced by half, two tablespoons shallots, one teaspoon honey, half teaspoon chili, two cups spinach and ¼ cup chives. Current four portions retained; original publisher 4–6 is a serving suggestion rather than a precise mass yield. Roast fat/richness is restored without cutting butter or honey.
processAndHandling: Roast aromatics/tubers → discard stems/garlic and bowl hot tubers; concurrently raw vinegar reduces by half and transfers to bowl with shallots/honey → clean dry saucepan browns butter/chili → careful whisk into acid bowl → warm spinach/chive toss and seasoning. No raw animal protein; separate clean leafy-produce tools when serving alongside poultry.
timing: Allow about 70 minutes as a prep-and-roast subtotal: roughly 10 minutes to prepare and start the roast, then about an hour in the oven. Load only once the oven reaches 375°F; any heating still needed after prep extends elapsed time. Sauce and finishing work overlap the roast, giving about 20 minutes active work. Larger reductions and extra sheets can take longer; half-volume vinegar and tender centers are the endpoints. No separate rest is required.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below; use within 3–4 days. Reheat leftovers to 165°F. Serve while warm for the fresh spinach/chive contrast. On reheating, the leaves soften further and the vinaigrette may separate; toss again to coat the softened pieces.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Wash the sunchokes under running water before cutting. Set out a rimmed baking sheet with room for a single layer, a small light-colored saucepan and a heatproof bowl for the vinegar mixture. Use additional sheets for a larger batch.

steps.title: Roast the sunchokes
steps.text: Toss {{ingredients}} on the baking sheet and spread without piling. Roast for about 1 hour, turning once and checking any unevenly browned areas, until golden and easily pierced through the center with a fork. Continue if the centers are firm. Discard the thyme stems and garlic after roasting, then transfer the hot sunchokes to a large bowl.

steps.title: Reduce the vinegar separately
steps.text: While the sunchokes roast, set out {{ingredients}}. Simmer the vinegar alone over moderate heat until reduced to half its starting volume: 2 tablespoons for the original ¼-cup batch, roughly 3 minutes in a small pan. Use the volume endpoint for scaled batches rather than multiplying the time. Transfer the reduction to the heatproof bowl; stir in the shallots and honey. Wipe the saucepan clean and dry before returning it to the heat.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.text: Set out {{ingredients}}. Melt the butter alone in the clean, dry saucepan over medium heat. Swirl and stir, watching the milk solids beneath the foam. As they turn golden brown and smell nutty, add the red pepper flakes briefly, then take the pan off the heat before the solids blacken. Let the vigorous bubbling subside and carefully whisk the browned butter, including the browned solids, into the vinegar mixture in the bowl. Do not attempt to brown butter in the vinegar. Re-whisk before dressing if it separates.

steps.title: Dress and serve warm
steps.text: Set out {{ingredients}}. Add the spinach, chives and warm vinaigrette to the hot sunchokes and toss to coat. The spinach should soften against the warm vegetables, though it need not wilt completely. Taste, then season with the finishing salt and pepper. Serve warm with the chives distributed through the dish.

changedFields.before:
## Chef's Note

Sunchokes (Jerusalem artichokes) require a long roast at 375°F - about 60 minutes - to transform their inulin-heavy starch into a creamy, artichoke-like texture. Browning butter until it smells nutty (the French call this beurre noisette), then whisking it into reduced cider vinegar creates a savory-sweet glaze. The tangy vinegar cuts through the earthy sunchokes and rich brown butter.

## Directions

1.  **Roast:** Preheat oven to 375°F. Toss sunchokes with oil, thyme, garlic, and salt. Roast for 1 hour, flipping once, until golden and fork-tender. Discard herbs/garlic.
2.  **Reduce:** In a small pan, simmer cider vinegar until reduced to 2 tbsp (about 3 mins). Stir in shallots and honey.
3.  **Brown Butter:** In the same pan, melt butter over medium heat. Cook for 2 minutes until foamy, then add the chili flakes to bloom for the final minute until the butter is dark brown and fragrant. Whisk immediately into the vinegar mixture.
4.  **Bind:** Toss the hot sunchokes with the fresh spinach - the heat will wilt the leaves perfectly.
5.  **Finish:** Drizzle with the brown butter vinaigrette and top with chives for the mandatory **High Note**.
changedFields.after:
## Chef's Note

Roast the sunchokes until their centers are tender, then dress them with nutty brown butter, reduced cider vinegar, shallots and honey. Reduce the vinegar into a separate bowl and clean the saucepan before browning the butter; keeping those stages separate lets the milk solids brown instead of simmering in acid. Spinach and chives bring a fresh finish to the warm vegetables.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Heat the oven to 375°F. Wash the sunchokes under running water before cutting. Set out a rimmed baking sheet with room for a single layer, a small light-colored saucepan and a heatproof bowl for the vinegar mixture. Use additional sheets for a larger batch.
2. **Roast the sunchokes:** Toss sunchokes (Jerusalem artichokes), extra-virgin olive oil, fresh thyme sprigs, garlic cloves, and kosher salt on the baking sheet and spread without piling. Roast for about 1 hour, turning once and checking any unevenly browned areas, until golden and easily pierced through the center with a fork. Continue if the centers are firm. Discard the thyme stems and garlic after roasting, then transfer the hot sunchokes to a large bowl.
3. **Reduce the vinegar separately:** While the sunchokes roast, set out apple cider vinegar, shallots, and honey. Simmer the vinegar alone over moderate heat until reduced to half its starting volume: 2 tablespoons for the original ¼-cup batch, roughly 3 minutes in a small pan. Use the volume endpoint for scaled batches rather than multiplying the time. Transfer the reduction to the heatproof bowl; stir in the shallots and honey. Wipe the saucepan clean and dry before returning it to the heat.
4. **Brown the butter:** Set out unsalted butter and red pepper flakes. Melt the butter alone in the clean, dry saucepan over medium heat. Swirl and stir, watching the milk solids beneath the foam. As they turn golden brown and smell nutty, add the red pepper flakes briefly, then take the pan off the heat before the solids blacken. Let the vigorous bubbling subside and carefully whisk the browned butter, including the browned solids, into the vinegar mixture in the bowl. Do not attempt to brown butter in the vinegar. Re-whisk before dressing if it separates.
5. **Dress and serve warm:** Set out fresh spinach leaves, fresh chives, kosher salt, and black pepper. Add the spinach, chives and warm vinaigrette to the hot sunchokes and toss to coat. The spinach should soften against the warm vegetables, though it need not wilt completely. Taste, then season with the finishing salt and pepper. Serve warm with the chives distributed through the dish.
